texts.preamble: Joydeep Nath vs Unknown on 11 December, 2019 Author: Suvra Ghosh Bench: Suvra Ghosh
texts.facts: The petitioner in the present revisional application challenges the order dated 25th March, 2019 passed by the learned 3rd Metropolitan and Municipal Magistrate, Kolkata, in connection with Complaint Case No. 6D of 2010 under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 12/7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the petitioner filed an application before the learned Trial Court under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking permission to be represented through his learned advocate. The said petition was turned down by the learned Trial Court, against which the petitioner preferred revision. In disposing of the revisional application, the learned revisional Court directed the learned Magistrate to rehear the petition under section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and to pass appropriate order. The petition was moved afresh before the learned Trial Court and by the impugned order, the learned Trial Court rejected the said application.
texts.arguments: The learned advocate for the petitioner has referred to a photocopy of a document which suggests that the petitioner is the Director of several companies. In opposing the prayer of the petitioner, the opposite party submits that allowing an application under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is the discretionary power of the Court. In fact, no serious objection was raised by the opposite party against the petition under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is envisaged in Section 205(1) of the Code that - "Whenever a Magistrate issues a summons, he may, if he sees reason so to do, Joydeep Nath vs Unknown on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25356930/ 1 dispense with the personal attendance of the accused and permit him to appear by his pleader." In the present case, it prima facie appears that the petitioner is a Director of several companies and it is the case of the petitioner that he has to travel extensively due to his business commitments.
